For every complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its measurable Borel structure, every globally C^2 f:E->R, real kappa,h and natural J, assume kappa>=1,J>=2,h>0,and for every base point z and vector v in E,
  (1/(2kappa))||v||^2 <= D^2 f(z)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
For indices in Fin(J)={0,...,J-1},define exactly
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j=the real Lagrange cardinal polynomial at these nodes,
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)|:s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i}(t_i-s)ell_j(s)ds,
  b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s)ds,
  c_j=integral_0^h(h-s)ell_j(s)ds.
The node quotient uses real coercions;integrals are ordinary Lebesgue Bochner interval integrals and the supremum is real. If h Lambda<=1/(65536 kappa),define a=exp(-h/2),sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)),and for incoming z=(X,P) and supplied common vector pair zeta=(u,v),
  P0(z,zeta)=a P+sigma u,
  Y0_j(z,zeta)=X+t_j P0(z,zeta),
  Y1_i(z,zeta)=Y0_i(z,zeta)-sum_j omega_ij grad f(Y0_j(z,zeta)),
  Phi(z,zeta)=(X+h P0(z,zeta)-sum_j c_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)),
               a(P0(z,zeta)-sum_j b_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)))+sigma v).
Let Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2. Then for every z,zprime,zeta in E x E,
  sqrt(Q_kappa(Phi(z,zeta).1-Phi(zprime,zeta).1,
               Phi(z,zeta).2-Phi(zprime,zeta).2))
    <= (1-h/(65536 kappa))sqrt(Q_kappa(z.1-zprime.1,z.2-zprime.2)).
Square roots are nonnegative real square roots. Both compared updates use the same arbitrary zeta,pointwise with no noise-law or almost-everywhere restriction. All sums use J actual nodes. The contraction is in the displayed square-root quadratic energy with its cross term,rather than in an unstated Euclidean or maximum product norm. The statement contains no probability law,kernel assertion,transport-of-measures conclusion,iteration history or query-count claim.
